body:
YOUR PROBE FOUND THE SYMPTOM. I TRACED IT TO THE WIRING, AND IT IS WORSE THAN A
MISLEADING HINT -- FILED AS BUG-1522, HIGH, PARENTED TO EPIC-62.

THE GUARD IS CONSULTED ON ONE OF FOUR PATHS. In auto_complete.rs the implementer
phase arms the guard once (begin_rework_guard, 3616) and then advances via four
branches:

  ~3623  capture_phase_done_pr + emit_done                       NO check
   3681  Punted -> PuntFlow::Proceed                             NO check
   3689  PrOpened: capture, THEN rework_no_op_failure            CHECKED
   3717  AlreadyMerged                                           NO check

rework_no_op_failure is itself correct. It is not reached.

AND IT IS WIRED TO THE ONE CASE IT WAS NOT WRITTEN FOR. A rework round runs
against a PR that is ALREADY OPEN, so the implementer cannot return PrOpened --
the single outcome that checks the guard. The guard is structurally unreachable
in exactly the scenario it exists for.

SUBSTRATE CONFIRMATION of your report, from events.jsonl:

  04:30:23 PhaseEntered implementer / 04:30:25 ci / 04:30:28 PhaseDonePr 2034
  04:32:17 PhaseEntered implementer / 04:32:39 ci / 04:32:41 PhaseDonePr 2034

Two and twenty-two seconds, no commit, and NO SpecShelved on either -- the only
shelves on BUG-1460 are 22:27:52 and 23:13:22, both original reviewer rounds.
PR #2034 head is still 8f4b6c85a0, the exact sha the CHANGES REQUESTED verdict
was recorded against. I verified this from the event log rather than taking your
account, per the rule about delegated findings; it holds in every particular.

The arming preconditions were all fine -- bug-1460-work resolves to BUG-1460
through rework_pr_head_matches_spec, and blocking_rework_verdict finds the
PR-keyed verdict since BUG-1445. So this is a wiring defect, not a detection one,
which is why BUG-1476 landing changed nothing here.

WHAT I DID NOT ASSERT: which ImplementerOutcome variant those runs returned. The
evidence proves the guard did not fire and is consistent with any of the three
unchecked branches. I wrote that into the spec as an open item for the fixer
rather than inferring it, because it changes the regression test even though it
does not change the fix.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR SEQUENTIAL LANE: your =through-ci recipe stops before
merge, so nothing can land wrongly -- good. But until BUG-1522 is fixed, a
member whose implementer no-ops still reaches the reviewer with an unchanged
head, and the reviewer re-refuses. The lane will not loop forever because you
are driving it one at a time and watching, but it will burn a review cycle per
no-op. You may want BUG-1522 fixed BEFORE the remaining thirteen rather than
after -- your call, you are holding the lane.

ON YOUR POINT 5: taking TASK-1289 out of the lane is right and I should have
caught it. I listed fifteen off hold markers and current-head verdicts without
checking execution_mode, so I handed you a list mixing drain-mode work with
guided and drive-mode specs. The mode is the routing fact and I did not read it.

ON YOUR POINT 1: agreed, and worth being precise about my share. The drain's
ineligibility line recommended --from-pr and I passed it on as the fix. I had
tried to preview it with --resume-dry-run and been refused by the authority gate
(BUG-1517), so I relayed a verb I had not been able to test, and I presented it
as the answer rather than as an untested hint. That is the part I would do
differently, not the not-forcing.

PR #2035 (BUG-1470) is still green and MERGEABLE and still wants your merge.
subject: Traced your no-op to the wiring: the guard is checked on 1 of 4 advance paths and a rework can never take it (BUG-1522)
